item.title: T.I. and Tiny’s Legal Win Capped at $18 Million Following Latest OMG Girlz Doll Trial
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to Trending on Billboard, I'm your host. Today, we're diving into the latest development in the long-running legal battle between T.I., Tameka "Tiny" Harris, and toy company MGA.
[Music transitions]
Host: The power couple has been fighting MGA over their teen pop group OMG Girlz, claiming that the company's "O.M.G." dolls ripped off the group's name, outfits, and style. After a series of trials, T.I. and Tiny were awarded $18 million in damages, but they were seeking additional punitive damages, arguing that MGA's infringement was intentional and malicious.
[Short music break]
Host: However, a federal jury has rejected their request, capping the verdict at $18 million. The Harrises' attorneys have expressed disappointment in the verdict, stating that MGA's policies are inadequate to prevent intellectual property infringement. Despite this setback, T.I. and Tiny are still walking away with millions of dollars.
[Music transitions]
Host: This marks the fourth trial in six years of litigation over the O.M.G. dolls. The case has seen its fair share of twists and turns, including a mistrial, a wiped verdict, and an appeal. The Harrises' lawyers have vowed to continue fighting for their clients' rights and the rights of all creatives.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in to Trending on Billboard. We'll keep you updated on any future developments in this case. Until next time, stay tuned!
[Outro music continues to play]
